localFestivals.name: Hamaka Festival
localFestivals.description: A week-long cultural and thanksgiving festival in Taytay to celebrate the garments and woodworking industries of the town. The event showcases the garments and woodworking industries, with which aided the town to rise up from the ravages of war and continue to prosper since then. Furthermore, it is a celebration of creativity, artistry, and craftsmanship and talent of its people through job fair, sports, cooking contest, competitions, socio-civic activities fashion show, religious events, concerts, talent competitions, beauty pageants, variety show, and Liberation Day.

localFestivals.name: Feast of St. John the Baptist
localFestivals.description: The grandest celebration in Taytay, honoring the town's patron saint, St. John the Baptist. The week-long festivities include religious processions, street dancing, parades, cultural shows, beauty pageants, and the traditional basaan (water-splashing) on the feast day itself.

localFestivals.name: Tiangge Festival
localFestivals.description: A celebration of Taytay's identity as the Garments Capital of the Philippines. Features fashion shows, trade fairs, and special discounts at the famous Taytay Tiangge, drawing thousands of shoppers from across the country.

localFestivals.name: Araw ng Rizal
localFestivals.description: Provincial celebration to commemorate its founding anniversary, honoring Dr. José Rizal, the national hero and namesake of the Province of Rizal. Taytay participates with wreath-laying ceremonies and civic programs.

nationalHolidays.name: New Year's Day
nationalHolidays.description: First day of the new year.

nationalHolidays.name: Chinese New Year
nationalHolidays.description: Celebration of the Lunar New Year.

nationalHolidays.name: EDSA People Power Revolution Anniversary
nationalHolidays.description: Commemorates the peaceful 1986 revolution that restored democracy in the Philippines.

nationalHolidays.name: Maundy Thursday
nationalHolidays.description: Thursday before Easter, a day of solemn religious observance.

nationalHolidays.name: Good Friday
nationalHolidays.description: Friday before Easter, marking the crucifixion of Jesus Christ.

nationalHolidays.name: Black Saturday
nationalHolidays.description: Saturday before Easter, a day of mourning and reflection.

nationalHolidays.name: Araw ng Kagitingan (Day of Valor)
nationalHolidays.description: Honors the bravery of Filipino and American soldiers during World War II, particularly the Fall of Bataan.

nationalHolidays.name: Labor Day
nationalHolidays.description: Celebrates the contributions of workers and the labor movement.

nationalHolidays.name: Independence Day
nationalHolidays.description: Commemorates the declaration of Philippine independence from Spain in 1898.

nationalHolidays.name: Ninoy Aquino Day
nationalHolidays.description: Honors Senator Benigno 'Ninoy' Aquino Jr., whose assassination catalyzed the People Power Revolution.

nationalHolidays.name: National Heroes Day
nationalHolidays.description: Honors all Filipino heroes who fought for the country's freedom and sovereignty.

nationalHolidays.name: All Saints' Day
nationalHolidays.description: A day to honor and remember departed loved ones. Filipinos traditionally visit cemeteries.

nationalHolidays.name: All Souls' Day
nationalHolidays.description: Continuation of remembrance for the faithful departed.

nationalHolidays.name: Bonifacio Day
nationalHolidays.description: Honors Andrés Bonifacio, founder of the Katipunan and Father of the Philippine Revolution.

nationalHolidays.name: Feast of the Immaculate Conception of Mary
nationalHolidays.description: Catholic holy day of obligation widely observed in the Philippines.

nationalHolidays.name: Christmas Day
nationalHolidays.description: Celebration of the birth of Jesus Christ. The Philippines has one of the longest Christmas seasons in the world.

nationalHolidays.name: Rizal Day
nationalHolidays.description: Commemorates the martyrdom of Dr. José Rizal, the national hero of the Philippines.

nationalHolidays.name: Last Day of the Year / New Year's Eve
nationalHolidays.description: The final day of the year, celebrated with family gatherings and festivities.
